- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.16 or 79.68), then corrects with a downward bias.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion toward recent low/high trends.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days for the first 10–15 days, then catches up or slightly overshoots.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices (e.g., 79+).
- When history contains a strong upward trend, model overreacts with a peak forecast, then underreacts in subsequent days.
- Forecast tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp drops or sudden spikes in true values.
- Model fails to capture the “rebound” effect after a sharp decline — often underestimates the recovery phase.
